title: Acoustic and Lexical Signals for Native Language Identification of Language Learners
abstract: arXiv:2610.32382v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Spoken native language (L1) identification for second language learners has traditionally relied on acoustic attributes of speech. Comparatively little attention has been paid to analysing speech transcripts for L1 traces. In this paper, we present a study of L1 identification using both speech and corresponding transcripts from a spoken learner English corpus. We compare a WavLM-based audio L1 classifier with a zero-shot GPT-4o classifier operating on transcripts and analyse their predictions across proficiency levels using a CEFR-balanced evaluation set. Our experiments show that the audio classifier outperforms the transcript-based approach overall when full transcripts are available, although their relative strengths vary with learner proficiency. translated_title: 面向语言学习者母语识别的声学与词汇信号
translated_abstract: 第二语言学习者的口语母语（L1）识别传统上依赖于语音的声学属性，而通过分析语音转写文本来探寻母语痕迹的研究关注相对较少。本文提出了一项利用口语学习者英语语料库中的语音及其对应转写文本进行母语识别的研究。我们将基于WavLM的音频母语分类器与在转写文本上运行的零样本GPT-4o分类器进行对比，并使用CEFR平衡的评估集在不同熟练度水平上分析二者的预测结果。实验表明，当完整转写文本可用时，音频分类器总体上优于基于转写文本的方法，但两者的相对优势随学习者熟练度而变化：音频方法在A1级别表现更好，而从A2到C1级别，在拥有完整转写文本的情况下文本方法表现更佳。基于转写文本的准确率通常随熟练度提高而上升，而声学性能则保持……（摘要原文在此处被截断）
tldr: 该研究首次将基于WavLM的音频分类器与零样本GPT-4o转写文本分类器相结合用于第二语言学习者的母语识别，发现音频方法在低熟练度（A1）时更优，而文本方法在中高熟练度（A2–C1）时更具优势。
en_tdlr: This study combines a WavLM-based audio classifier with a zero-shot GPT-4o transcript-based classifier for native language identification of L2 learners, showing that audio signals work better at low proficiency (A1) while lexical transcript signals excel at intermediate-to-high proficiency levels (A2–C1).
